qs.q: A young, thin female patient with drooping shoulders exhibits true neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome characterized by the classic Gilliatt-Sumner hand. Which intrinsic hand muscle experiences the most pronounced wasting in this specific presentation?
o: The abductor digiti minimi intrinsic hand muscle
The abductor pollicis brevis intrinsic hand muscle
The first dorsal interosseous intrinsic hand muscle
The first lumbrical intrinsic hand muscle
qs.e: True neurogenic TOS classically features the Gilliatt-Sumner hand, which shows prominent wasting of the abductor pollicis brevis with lesser involvement of the interossei and hypothenar muscles. Interossei wasting is more characteristic of ulnar neuropathy at the elbow.
qs.s: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome, Peritoneal Adhesions and Compartment: MCQs

qs.q: During hand biomechanics study, a student reviews the lumbrical muscles. What are the two primary actions of these intrinsic hand muscles?
o: Flex interphalangeal joints and extend metacarpophalangeal joints
Pronate and supinate the proximal phalanges of the hand
Extend interphalangeal joints and flex metacarpophalangeal joints
Abduct and adduct the fingers at the interphalangeal joints
qs.e: The lumbrical muscles flex the metacarpophalangeal joints and extend the interphalangeal joints. Their unique action helps coordinate delicate finger movements.
qs.s: PAT III — Progress Assessment Test (8 November 2019) — Revision Guide: MCQs

qs.q: A patient presents with an inability to oppose the thumb and sensory loss over the lateral palm and first three digits. Which of the following intrinsic hand muscles is NOT supplied by the median nerve or its branches?
qs.e: The adductor pollicis is supplied by the ulnar nerve, whereas the other listed muscles are innervated by the median nerve. Opponens pollicis and the lateral lumbricals receive median nerve innervation.
